title: JB Charleston Multiple Award Construction Contract
description: THIS SOLICITATION IS ISSUED AS A COMPETITIVE HUBZone AND SDVOSB BUSINESS SET-ASIDE USING TRADE-OFF PROCEDURES AND THE PROVISIONS OF SECTIONS L & M. NOTICE TO OFFEROR(S)/SUPPLIER(S): FUNDS ARE NOT PRESENTLY AVAILABLE FOR THIS EFFORT. NO AWARD WILL BE MADE UNDER THIS SOLICITATION UNTIL FUNDS ARE AVAILABLE. THE GOVERNMENT RESERVES THE RIGHT TO CANCEL THIS SOLICITATION, EITHER BEFORE OR AFTER THE CLOSING DATE. IN THE EVENT THE GOVERNMENT CANCELS THIS SOLICITATION, THE GOVERNMENT HAS NO OBLIGATION TO REIMBURSE AN OFFEROR FOR ANY COSTS. Multiple Award Construction Contract (MACC) to support the construction program at Joint Base Charleston (JB CHS). JB CHS encompasses the following locations: Joint Base Charleston - Air Base, Charleston, SC; Joint Base Charleston - Weapons Station, Goose Creek, SC; Short Stay Recreational Area, Moncks Corner, SC; North Auxiliary Airfield, North, SC; Defense Fuel Supply Point, Charleston, SC. In addition, MACC vendors will support Seymour Johnson AFB and Shaw AFB for emergency use. The type of work vendors can expect will include, but is not limited to, new construction, alteration/repair and/or demolition of buildings and structures, roads, grounds, and utilities. Work may also include design/build from concept to full 100% design. Vendors will furnish all materials, equipment, transportation, and personnel necessary for project requirements and to manage and accomplish multiple, simultaneous projects.

title: FY26 NPTU High-Pressure Air Compressors (HPAC) Mx
description: The Nuclear Power Training Unit (NPTU) requires a major maintenance overhaul of its High-Pressure Air (AHP) System to maintain operational reliability, readiness, and mission support. To sustain critical operations, the multi-stage AHP compressors require an 8,000-hour major overhaul, encompassing complete teardown, component replacement, tolerance verification, and re-certification. The Contractor shall provide all labor, certified replacement parts, tooling, and test equipment necessary to execute the 8,000-hour major overhaul on the designated AHP compressors. All maintenance, inspections, and re-certification procedures shall be performed strictly in accordance with Maintenance Requirement Card (MRC) AHP-R-2 (Rev 3) (Attachment 02). Maintenance actions must be phased to ensure continuous, redundant compressor availability throughout the period of performance. Please be advised that the full requirements, including Instructions to Offerors (FAR 52.212-1) and the basis for evaluation (FAR 52.212-2), are detailed in the solicitation attachments. A thorough review of all attached documents is required for a compliant submission.

title: Echocardiogram Services
description:
Gloucestershire Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust (GHFT) is seeking to procure additional echocardiography capacity to address a significant backlog in diagnostic services. Current waiting times for echocardiograms exceed the national DM01 standard of six weeks. The Trust intends to establish a two-year call-off contract, with the option to extend for up to a further two years in two separate one-year increments (1+1), to support backlog reduction and improve timely patient access to services. The contract start date is estimated to be 1st April 2027.

Suppliers must be able to deliver echocardiography services in line with the Trust’s specification and clinical requirements, ensuring compliance with relevant quality, governance, and service standards.

title: I Storm Membership � Notice of Intent to Sole Source
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) intends to award a sole source Firm Fixed Price contract for an organizational membership to I-STORM (The International Network for Storm Surge Barriers) to support the operation, lifecycle maintenance, and engineering design of critical coastal flood risk management assets. I-Storm is the international network for storm surge barriers that is an international knowledge base sharing network for all who study storm surge barrier industry. Storm barriers are frequently the first line of defense against rising tides. The barriers are being developed around the world to reduce risk of severe flooding to people and property. Period of Performance: One year. A solicitation will not be posted. However, any firm that believes it can meet this requirement may give written notification to the Contracting Officer by 21 September 2026. Supporting evidence must be in sufficient detail to demonstrate the ability to comply with the requirement. Responses received will be evaluated. However, a determination by the Government to compete the proposed procurement based on the responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. If no responses are received, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers will proceed with awarding a Firm Fixed contract to I-STORM (The International Network for Storm Surge Barriers).

title: PTAG RFI: USPTO seeks Real Estate Planning & Management Support Services
description: ***9/15/26 AMENDED: Since the answers to the questions received are still being compiled. the deadline has been extended to MONDAY, SEPTEMBER 15, 2026 AT 1:00 PM ET*** ***9/4/26 AMENDED: in Acknowledgement of the holiday weekend, the deadline for questions has been extended to WEDNESDAY, SEPTEMBER 9, 2026 AT 1:00 PM ET*** THIS IS A PTAG SOURCES SOUGHT REQUEST FOR INFORMATION (RFI) ONLY. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS: 531210 - Offices of Real Estate Agents and Brokers and PSC R499 - SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) The USPTO Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), seeks a contractor to provide real estate portfolio management support services to include real property planning support and to assist the USPTO on all negotiations and discussions related to its GSA leasehold interests for the Alexandria Campus and Detroit Regional Office. In addition, support may be requested to assist the USPTO to make long-term planning decisions for each of the facilities within the USPTO�s portfolio. Currently, these facilities include the Dallas Regional Office located in a GSA owned facility; and the San Jose Regional Office which is directly leased by the USPTO. Real property planning support is required for all USPTO�s real property holdings. USPTO, as a tenant, must develop and implement a real estate portfolio strategy to secure, right-size, and maintain agency space needs without disruption. This contract will enable USPTO to mitigate resource constraints and improve efficiency, while securing technical data and expertise to ensure the implementation of an effective real property strategy going forward. Current Office Locations Main campus headquarters: 600 Dulany Street, Alexandria Virginia which is GSA leased space for which USPTO has separate occupancy agreements for each of the following buildings: Madison East/ Madison West , Knox, and Jefferson. USPTO directly leases one garage structure (East Garage) housing 1780 parking spaces directly connected to the main campus A GSA leased warehouse in Lorton VA. GSA owned warehouse in Springfield VA. Current Regional Offices: Detroit RO: 300 River Place, Detroit, Michigan. GSA leased space Dallas RO: 207 S. Houston St, Dallas, Texas. GSA owned facility San Jose RO: 200 E. Santa Clara St, San Jose, California. The response to this RFI should provide OCAO management with an understanding of the contractor�s experience and the range of services provided. This will allow USPTO to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE All interested contractors should provide the following information in their response via e-mail to the contacts listed below: The name of your contractor, address, SAM UEI, point of contact information, email, phone, website address. Your FSS Schedule contract number (Only if applicable). Proof your contractor is a small business under NAICS 531210 Any relevant certifications or other relevant authorizations Information about your contractor�s ability to meet the requirements stated above by providing enough detail to show: Past performance should include twenty plus years of real estate analysis and planning experience with the GSA policies and procedures and engagement in the areas of space strategies, POR requirements, and lease negotiations. Understanding of current USPTO space standards, business units, regional functionality and operations, and unique staff requirements as it pertains to the various unions. Demonstrated experience with federal government real estate policy, procurement process, federal government program of requirements development, leveraging experience with the GSA, evaluation practices and lease negotiations. Demonstrated expertise in working with the GSA, OMB and Congress for federal office space leasing acquisition. Expert level experience in strategic planning and programming, conceptual and schematic design, design development, construction and contract documents, and project administration. Key Personnel In your response to this source sought, please identify any Key Personnel that would likely be involved in fulfilling the requirements, and include any relevant background information on those individuals. QUESTIONS Questions regarding this RFI are due no later than September 9. 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via eBUY and/or email to Kendall.jones1@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov NO PHONE CALLS PLEASE DEADLINE: Responses are due no later than Monday, September 21. 2026 at 1:00 PM ET and are to be submitted via eBUY and/or email to Kendall.jones1@uspto.gov and christopher.ward@uspto.gov Late responses may be considered at the government�s discretion. Disclaimer: This PTAG Sources Sought Request For Information (RFI) notice is issued solely for Market Research information and planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation. All information received in response to this RFI that is marked as proprietary will be handled in accordance with procurement integrity requirements. Responses to this notice are not offers and cannot be accepted by the Government to form a binding contract. Responders are solely responsible for all expenses associated with responding to this RFI.

title: 9 OSS ATC Window Shades
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with RFO part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation. Offers are being requested and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. FA468626QC011 is issued as a Request for Quote (RFQ). This acquisition is a 100% small business set-aside. This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. (ii). A list of line item number(s) and items, quantities, and units of measure is identified in Attachment 1 - Solicitation, Under Supplies or Services & Prices or Costs. Offerors shall return completed pricing as part of their quote submission. (iii). Beale Air Force Base (AFB) Air Traffic Control (ATC) Tower sunshades are worn and require total replacement due to natural aging and environmental exposure. FAA Order 6480.18 recommends replacement every 5 to 7 years. The existing Beale AFB tower cab shades have not been replaced since 2017 and exhibit advanced material degradation, crazing, and roller tension failure. In accordance with Attachment 2: FAA Master Specification Section 12 25 12 (ATCT Transparent Plastic Window Shades) and FAA-E-2470b, control cab window treatments must maintain optical clarity and uniform light filtering. Continued degradation creates an active flight safety hazard by subjecting air traffic controllers to uncontrolled solar glare and visual impairment during critical flightline operations. (iv). Date(s) and place(s) of delivery and acceptance and FOB point is identified in Attachment 1 - Solicitation, Under Deliveries or Performance Schedules. Place of Contract Performance: Beale AFB, CA; Period of Performance: All delivery and installation must be completed between 30 September 2026 and 30 November 2026, executed within the operational safety windows specified in the SON. (v). The provision at 52.212-1, Instructions to Offerors-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition. The provision at 52.212-2, Evaluation-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition and the specific evaluation criteria to be included is identified in Attachment 1. (vi). Offerors shall include a completed copy of the provision at 52.212-3, Offeror Representations and Certifications-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, with its offer. The clause at 52.212-4, Contract Terms and Conditions-Commercial Products and Commercial Services, applies to this acquisition. (vii). The Contractor shall provide a minimum five (5) year standard commercial warranty from the date of final Government acceptance covering all manufacturer defects, in accordance with FAA-E-2470b. (viii). Response Times: Q&A's are due Thursday, 17 September 2026 @ 10:00AM PST to the POCs listed below. Offers are due Monday, 21 September 2026 @ 10:00AM PST to the POCs listed below. The name and telephone number of the individual(s) to contact for information regarding the solicitation is Contracting Officer - Teresa Romig, teresa.romig@us.af.mil and Contract Specialist, SrA Ezekiel Onumah, ezekiel.onumah.1@us.af.mil.

Technical Acceptability The technical quote will be evaluated to verify submission of the required authorized reseller/distributor documentation. Price, and price alone, will be the deciding factor. Award will be made to the lowest-priced Offeror whose technical quote is rated Acceptable. Evaluation Sequence To maximize efficiency, the Government may evaluate price first. The technical quote of the lowest-priced Offeror will then be evaluated. The Government reserves the right to evaluate all quotes or hold discussions if determined to be in the Government�s best interest. Offeror-imposed terms and conditions that deviate from the Government�s material requirements may result in an Unacceptable rating. PRICE EVALUATION APPROACH Firm Fixed Price The Government will evaluate offers by totaling all line-item prices, including options. In accordance with FAR 52.217-8, evaluation will also include an additional 6-month option period priced using the final option period rates. Base year, option periods, and the additional 6-month extension will be summed to determine the Total Evaluated Price. Award will be made to the Lowest Price Technically Acceptable Offeror in accordance with RFO Part 12. Responses should contain your best terms, conditions. This PTAG 6.1.1 Sources Sought (request for information) Notice (RFI) is strictly for market research ONLY. It is for informational and planning purposes and shall NOT be construed as a solicitation or as an obligation or commitment by the Government at this time. PTAG The Government contemplates utilizing the Alternative Competition Method in accordance with the Patent and Trademark Office Acquisition Guidelines (PTAG) and the Patent and Trademark Office Efficiency Act 35 U.S.C. 2(b)(4)(A). This Sources sought notice is intended as preliminary market information gathering which the United States patent and Trademark Office (USPTO) will use to determine which small business contractor(s) is/are the most likely to successfully meet the agency�s needs and are thereby eligible to participate in an alternative competition. As a result of this market research, the solicitation will only be issued to the/ those qualified small business contractor(s) that is/are deemed most likely to successfully meet the agency�s requirements as stated below. This RFI is being made available under NAICS: 531210 - Offices of Real Estate Agents and Brokers and PSC R499 - SUPPORT- PROFESSIONAL: OTHER Purpose of this Sources Sought / Request for Information (RFI) The USPTO Office of the Chief Administrative Officer (OCAO), seeks a contractor to provide real estate portfolio management support services to include real property planning support and to assist the USPTO on all negotiations and discussions related to its GSA leasehold interests for the Alexandria Campus and Detroit Regional Office. In addition, support may be requested to assist the USPTO to make long-term planning decisions for each of the facilities within the USPTO�s portfolio. Currently, these facilities include the Dallas Regional Office located in a GSA owned facility; and the San Jose Regional Office which is directly leased by the USPTO. Real property planning support is required for all USPTO�s real property holdings. USPTO, as a tenant, must develop and implement a real estate portfolio strategy to secure, right-size, and maintain agency space needs without disruption. This contract will enable USPTO to mitigate resource constraints and improve efficiency, while securing technical data and expertise to ensure the implementation of an effective real property strategy going forward. Current Office Locations Main campus headquarters: 600 Dulany Street, Alexandria Virginia which is GSA leased space for which USPTO has separate occupancy agreements for each of the following buildings: Madison East/ Madison West , Knox, and Jefferson. USPTO directly leases one garage structure (East Garage) housing 1780 parking spaces directly connected to the main campus A GSA leased warehouse in Lorton VA. GSA owned warehouse in Springfield VA. Current Regional Offices: Detroit RO: 300 River Place, Detroit, Michigan. GSA leased space Dallas RO: 207 S. Houston St, Dallas, Texas. GSA owned facility San Jose RO: 200 E. Santa Clara St, San Jose, California. The response to this RFI should provide OCAO management with an understanding of the contractor�s experience and the range of services provided. This will allow USPTO to conduct thorough market research, identify suitable providers, and make informed decisions. HOW TO RESPOND TO THIS SOURCES SOUGHT NOTICE All interested contractors should provide the following information in their response via e-mail to the contacts listed below: The name of your contractor, address, SAM UEI, point of contact information, email, phone, website address. Your FSS Schedule contract number (Only if applicable). Understanding of current USPTO space standards, business units, regional functionality and operations, and unique staff requirements as it pertains to the various unions. Demonstrated experience with federal government real estate policy, procurement process, federal government program of requirements development, leveraging experience with the GSA, evaluation practices and lease negotiations. Demonstrated expertise in working with the GSA, OMB and Congress for federal office space leasing acquisition. Expert level experience in strategic planning and programming, conceptual and schematic design, design development, construction and contract documents, and project administration. Key Personnel In your response to this source sought, please identify any Key Personnel that would likely be involved in fulfilling the requirements, and include any relevant background information on those individuals. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested and a written solicitation will not be issued. The Department of War (DoW) intends to negotiate on a sole source basis with Siemens Industry Inc for the procurement of services for Test Support Equipment Control and Monitoring Systems at Edwards AFB. NOTICE OF INTENT TO SOLE SOURCE Statutory Authority RFO 12.201-1 and 41 U.S.C. 1901 Justification The TSECMS software is proprietary software from Siemens Inc. and therefore they are they only vendor with the capability to perform the necessary maintenance and provide support and upgrades. Only Siemens specialists have access to the use of the service tools, technical service bulletins and system software updates required to ensure proper operation of the Building Automation and HVAC system. Siemens provided a sole source letter stating " The Siemens Building Automation System (Siemens Apogee) installed at Edwards BAF uses hardware and software unique and proprietary to Siemens for operation of the facility's environmental system. The services provided under the service agreement to maintain the installed Siemens HVAC control systems at Edwards BAF are best provided by Siemens factory trained service technicians. Only Siemens specialists have access to the of the service tools, technical service bulletins and system software updates required to ensure proper operation of the Building Automation and HVAC system. The maintained equipment is very technical in nature and requires service and support specific to Siemens manufactured equipment provided by dedicated Siemens specialists under the proposed agreement. Moreover, Siemens Building Automation System software support and updates, and online and onsite support for emergency and non-emergency situations are only available through the local Siemens office and warranty coverage is contingent on proper maintenance by factory trained Siemens personnel." Additionally, during market research, the agency evaluated assertions from an interested small business that the TSECMS requirement could be maintained by procuring software licenses and hardware commodities commercially from GSA Schedules. In coordination with the OEM, Siemens Industry, Inc., the Government conducted an in-depth technical analysis and determined this approach is technically unviable and introduces unacceptable mission risk for the following reasons: 1. Proprietary Diagnostic Tool Exclusivity (Comtool): The TSECMS infrastructure across Buildings 1020, 1030, and 1040 comprises approximately 95% legacy field controller architecture (including PXCM, PXCC, MBC, and MEC panels) integrated with Apogee Insight and Desigo CC databases. Proper commissioning, baseline maintenance, HMI access, and firmware patching on these legacy panels require the Siemens-proprietary Comtool. This diagnostic software utility is tightly controlled, not public-facing, and is legally and technically restricted to direct Siemens factory personnel. Third-party contractors and Value Added Partners (VAPs) only have access to the commercial TALON Configurator, which is incompatible with the legacy Siemens panels installed at Edwards AFB. Non-OEM entities possess no technical means to interface with or configure these baseline controllers. 2. Inaccessibility of Core Diagnostic & System Assessment Utilities: Beyond basic software seats, executing the Performance Work Statement requires proprietary internal utilities�including ZoneRX, Datafox, and ChalkTalk (Demand Flow Smart Services)�as well as internal Siemens diagnostic scripts used to analyze deep-level system faults and reset hardware timers. These tools are proprietary intellectual property of Siemens, are not distributed via GSA Schedules or third-party distribution channels, and are accessible only to factory-certified OEM technicians. 3. Life Safety, Emergency Response, and Hardware Lead Times (B-416195): Control loop failures within the Anechoic Chamber testing environment present direct life-safety risks to personnel and mission-critical assets, as demonstrated by a historical thermal failure reaching 150�F. Immediate mitigation requires localized parts availability. Standard commercial GSA procurement involves variable and extended supply-chain lead times. Conversely, a direct OEM service agreement includes dedicated local warehouse inventory and secure onsite staging under lock-and-key, ensuring compliance with mandatory emergency response thresholds. 4. Absence of Tier-3 Escalation and Voided Labor Warranties: Siemens confirmed that third-party maintenance voids OEM engineering support and material warranties. In the event of a catastrophic control failure affecting active aircraft testing, third-party contractors have no contractual or technical mechanism to command Tier-3 OEM engineering escalation. Based on this integrated market analysis, the Government concludes that Siemens is the only responsible source capable of fulfilling the complete, unified scope of the TSECMS requirement without causing unacceptable delays or mission failure. The contract must be sole-sourced to Siemens to protect system integrity. Scope of Work The contractor shall provide Services in accordance with Performance of Work Statement Attached. Market Research Internet searches, government databases, and a sources sought posting were all utilized to find alternate vendors for the required service. However, after in-depth review of two vendors' capability statements, it was concluded that Siemens holds the proprietary items for the existing TSECMS system. Attempting to compete the requirement�which would result in a small business prime contractor performing only partial aspects of the scope while relying on Siemens for proprietary access�would severely complicate the requirement. Because the physical hardware, mechanical systems, and proprietary controls software are digitally integrated, splitting the maintenance or introducing an unauthorized third party would create split system liability and a "finger-pointing" environment. If a critical failure were to occur during active aircraft test support operations, the government would suffer from unacceptable mission delays, voided OEM warranties, and a lack of a single point of accountability to resolve the failure. Therefore, the requirement must remain unified and sole-sourced to Siemens. Additionally, during market research, the agency evaluated assertions from an interested small business that the TSECMS requirement could be maintained by procuring software licenses and hardware commodities commercially from GSA Schedules. In coordination with the OEM, Siemens Industry, Inc., the Government conducted an in-depth technical analysis and determined this approach is technically unviable and introduces unacceptable mission risk for the reasons stated above. Instructions to Interested Parties This notice of intent is not a request for competitive proposals; however, all responsible sources may submit a capability statement, proposal, or quotation which shall be considered by the agency. A determination by the Government not to compete this proposed contract based upon responses to this notice is solely within the discretion of the Government. title: Lackland Laundry and Linen
description: UPDATED TO INCLUDE Q&A's. New Closing date of 21 Sep 2026. Combined Synopsis/Solicitation for Lackland Laundry & Linen Services Solicitation Number: HT9408-26-Q-E029 Agency: Defense Health Agency Contracting Activity (DHACA), Healthcare Contracting Division - South (HCD-S) Classification Code: S209 - Housekeeping - Laundry/Drycleaning NAICS Code: 812320 - Drycleaning and Laundry Services (except Coin-Operated) Set-Aside: 100% Small Business (SBA Size Standard: $8.0 Million) Response Due Date: September 21, 2026, 12:00 PM Central Standard Time Place of Performance: Services will be performed for the Wilford Hall Ambulatory Surgical Center (WHASC) and other outlying clinics at Joint Base San Antonio (JBSA) Lackland and JBSA Randolph, Texas. Description of Services: The Defense Health Agency is seeking a contractor to provide all necessary personnel, equipment, supplies, facilities, and transportation for non-personal, medical-grade bulk laundry and dry-cleaning services. This is a competitive follow-on to Blanket Purchase Agreement (BPA) HT940823A0002. The required services include, but are not limited to: Bulk medical laundry processing, sorting, and delivery. Microfiber laundry services. Special item laundry services for non-standard clinical linens and lab coats. Specialized stain wash services for heavily soiled linens. Veterinary laundry services, kept separate from human clinical linens. Bulk laundry services for the JBSA Randolph Clinic. The contractor must adhere to strict quality control, infection control, and transportation standards, including guidelines from the CDC, OSHA, and the Healthcare Laundry Accreditation Council (HLAC). This includes maintaining specific air pressure boundaries in processing facilities and following sanitation protocols for transport vehicles. The Government will award a single, Firm-Fixed-Price contract. The award will be made to the responsible offeror whose proposal is compliant, receives a "Pass" for Technical Capability, and represents the Best Value to the Government based on a comparative tradeoff between Past Performance and Price. title: Wiley Journals
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial services prepared in accordance with the commercial procedures of the Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) Part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a written solicitation document will not be issued. This solicitation is issued as an RFQ, 36C77626Q0090. The solicitation document and incorporated provisions and clauses are those in effect through Federal Acquisition Circular 2026-01. This acquisition is a total set aside for Service-Disabled Veteran Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSBs). This solicitation incorporates provisions and clauses by reference. The full text of provisions and clauses may be accessed electronically at www.acquisition.gov. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 519290, with a small business size standard of 1,000 employees. The FSC/PSC is R605. The Department of Veterans Affairs, Regional Procurement Office-Central, 1639 Medical Center Parkway, Suite 204, Murfreesboro, TN 371291 is seeking an existing, commercial, off-the-shelf, web-based electronic collection of Wiley Journals as outlined in Attachment D.1. INSTRUCTIONS TO QUOTERS (A) Volume I � Technical - Quotes shall clearly and completely address the appropriate technical areas of consideration described below in a format that follows the Statement of Work (SOW) deliverables. Responses to these items will form the basis for the technical merits of each quote. (B) Volume II � Price - The Offeror shall submit a firm-fixed price quote for all items described within the SOW. The Government will evaluate the price by adding the total of all line-item prices, including all options and an estimated cost to exercise FAR 52.217-8. The Total Evaluated Price will be that sum. (C) Documentation that reflects your entity is an authorized reseller/distributor of these journals from the publisher or intellectual property holder. FACTORS TO BE EVALUATED 1. Technical 2. Price The award will be made to the response most advantageous to the Government. Responses should contain your best terms, conditions. All Offerors are advised that, in the interest of efficiency, the Government reserves the right to conduct the evaluation in the most effective manner. Specifically, the Government may first evaluate the total proposed price of all Offerors. Thereafter, the Government will evaluate the technical quote of the lowest priced Offeror only. If the lowest priced Offeror�s technical quote is determined to be rated as Acceptable, the Government may make award to that Offeror without further evaluation of the remaining Offerors� technical quotes. If the lowest priced Offeror�s technical proposal is determined to be rated as Unacceptable, then the Government may evaluate the next lowest priced technical quote, and so forth and so on, until the Government reaches the lowest priced technical quote that is determined to be rated as acceptable. However, the Government reserves the right to evaluate all Offerors� technical quotes should it desire to conduct discussions, or otherwise determine it to be in the Government�s best interest. Please be advised that any Offeror-imposed terms and conditions which deviate from the Government�s material terms and conditions established by this solicitation may render the Offeror�s proposal Unacceptable and thus, ineligible for award. 1. TECHNICAL EVALUATION APPROACH The technical evaluation process will consider the following: (1) The evaluation process will consider whether the quote demonstrates a clear understanding of the technical features involved in meeting the solicitation requirements and whether the Offeror�s methods and approach have adequately and completely considered, defined, and satisfied the requirements in the Solicitation. 2. PRICE EVALUATION APPROACH Firm Fixed Price: The Government will evaluate offers by adding the total of all line-item prices, including all options. In addition, FAR 52.217-8, Option to Extend Services applies to this solicitation. As such, evaluation of options under FAR 52.217-8 will also include using the prices offered for the last option period to determine the price for an additional 6-month option period in the event an extension is issued under FAR 52.217-8. The Offeror�s proposed total base year price, total option period prices, and the additional 6-month option period price will then be added together to arrive at the Offeror�s Total Evaluated Price. The Total Evaluated Price will be that sum. Award will be based upon a comparative evaluation of quotes in accordance with RFO Part 12. Comparative evaluation is the side by side pairwise comparison of quotes based on factors resulting in a Contracting Officer decision for the quote most favorable to the Government. The award will be made to the response most advantageous to the Government. Responses should contain your best terms, conditions. To facilitate the award process, all quotes must include a statement regarding the terms and conditions herein as follows: "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document without modification, deletion, or addition." OR "The terms and conditions in the solicitation are acceptable to be included in the award document with the exception, deletion, or addition of the following:" Quoters shall list exception(s) and rationale for the exception(s), if any. System updates may lag policy updates. The System for Award Management (SAM) may continue to require entities to complete representations based on provisions that are not included in agency solicitations. Contracting officers will not consider these representations when making award decisions or enforce requirements. Entities are not required to, nor are they able to, update their entity registration to remove these representations in SAM. Questions regarding this solicitation shall be received not later than 9 AM EST, September 15, 2026, via email to Erich Hoffman, Erich.Hoffman@va.gov The deadline for submissions regarding this RFQ is 1:00PM EST, September 18, 2026, via email at erich.hoffman@va.gov . Quotations received after this date and time will not be reviewed. Phone calls will not be accepted. Late submissions shall be treated in accordance with the solicitation provision at RFO 52.212-1(f). Any questions or concerns regarding this solicitation should be forwarded in writing via e-mail to the Point of Contact listed below. Point of Contact Erich Hoffman, Contract Specialist Erich.Hoffman@va.gov

In accordance with RFO 12.201(c)(2), the U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) is soliciting quotes directly from suppliers for Concealable Body Armor T-Shirt Systems. This is a notice of intent only. A formal request for quote will not be published on SAM.gov. Set-aside: Full and Open NAICS Code: 315990 PSC: 8470 Description: The Contractor shall provide a complete concealable body armor T?shirt system consisting of a low?profile compression-style (T-Shirt) carrier, and front and back, NIJ?certified soft armor inserts (panels). All body armor provided under this contract shall meet or exceed, with documented evidence of compliance, the following: National Institute of Justice (NIJ) Standard 0101.06 Minimum protection level: Level IIIA Compliance with all applicable federal, state, and local regulations Body Armor System The body armor system shall: Provide ballistic protection that meets or exceeds NIJ Level IIIA in accordance with NIJ Standard 0101.06. Include 360-degree protective coverage, consisting of Front ballistic panel Rear ballistic panel Side ballistic panels or optional side expansion capability. Utilize polyethylene or aramid soft armor with multi?hit capability. Be engineered for covert wear, producing no visible outline (�printing�) when worn beneath standard civilian attire. Maintain full mobility while resisting panel folding, curling, or shifting during extended physical activity. The complete system shall provide ventilated, lightweight protection, not exceeding a reasonable weight threshold of 3 lbs. for all?day operational wear. Offer thin-profile armor panels, not exceeding 0.25�0.35 inches in thickness. Carrier Requirements The carrier shall: Be a compression-fit T?shirt style carrier specifically designed to secure armor panels close to the body. Feature breathable, sweat?wicking, and moisture?evaporating fabric suitable for daily operational use. Maintain panel retention pockets that correctly index ballistic panels and prevent sagging, twisting, or displacement. Provide reinforced stitching and durability suitable for repeated wash/wear cycles required by law?enforcement operations. Include elastic stabilization zones to reduce movement during running, defensive tactics, and vehicle operations. Be fully machine-washable with armor panels removed. Be available in neutral colors (e.g., black, white, grey) to support concealment. Materials used shall support covert operations and produce little to no sound signature when worn under clothing; hook-and-loop �Velcro�, raised snaps, clips, or other noisy fasteners are not permitted. Fit and Sizing Armor system shall be available in multiple sizes (S, M, L, XL, etc....) to ensure proper fit for all personnel Additional Features Hydrophobic panel casing to protect ballistic material from sweat and moisture. Abrasion?resistant outer panel skin to prolong service life. Heat?sealed seams on ballistic panels to prevent contamination or fiber intrusion. Delivery Requirements Delivery timelines: Within 30 days of order placement (or as negotiated) Deliveries shall be made to locations specified at the order level Items shall be packaged to prevent damage during transit Partial shipments must be approved by the Government

description: The FAA has a requirement for engineering services necessary to perform remedial investigation (RI), and remedial action (RA) activities at multiple Environmental Cleanup (ECU) Program sites and areas of concern (AOCs), at 16 different AOCs, at the former Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Station on Annette Island Reserve, Alaska. Special Considerations: - This project will be performed on the Annette Island Reserve which is under the authority of the Metlakatla Indian Community (MIC). Interested vendors must have had experience in the last 10 years with the regulations of the Metlakatla Indian Community Environmental Council as well as, experience working within the Metlakatla Indian Community policies for worker and business permits, as well as materials purchase. - MIC requires all visitors to apply for a visitor permit. Visitors who will be in the community for longer than two weeks will need to apply for a residency permit. - All excavation backfill material must be purchased from MIC. No organic materials, including seed mixes, can be brought to the island. - Global positioning system (GPS) service and telecommunications are unavailable in many areas on the Metlakatla Peninsula. Satellite communications, mobile GPS antenna stations, walkie-talkies, and/or other technology resources may be needed to verify target locations, allow for communications across Contractor teams and with FAA representatives, and ensure safety of the field team. - Most sites are historical in nature and no longer serve to support FAA�s National Airspace System (NAS). Most sites were abandoned and/or demolished by the FAA in the 1960s, 1970s, and 1980s. While significant clearing occurred at many of the target sites in 2023 and 2024, the Contractor should anticipate that considerable overgrowth (mostly alder and brush) or new growth is present at these sites. - The Contractor must abide by all applicable laws, codes, regulations, and guidance, and is required to perform all work in full compliance with federal, state (as applicable outside Annette Island), and local laws, codes, and regulations. The Contractor must ensure that all activities executed by their personnel, subcontractors, and suppliers are in full compliance with said laws, codes, regulations, and guidance. Any incident of noncompliance must immediately be brought to the attention of the FAA CO. Nothing in this SOW relieves the Contractor of their responsibility to comply with all applicable laws and regulations. - Prior projects encountered multiple issues due to the logistics of getting sample shipments off Annette Island and onto Gravina Island to be transported to the laboratory. The weather, airplane schedules, ferry schedules, staffing reductions and freight office closures at Alaska Airlines, can all impact the transportation of sample shipments. The 200mg/kg concentration for the MIC cleanup level for DRO and RRO makes the use of a PID/FID to screen excavations for boundary obtainment difficult. The matrix interference from organic materials, obtaining reliable usable analytical results to determine if an excavation has reached its boundary has been difficult to obtain in a reasonable timeframe. At times the laboratory data has not been usable due to matrix interference, holding time exceedance, or turnaround time delays. Summary Statement of Work: - The Contractor must submit a Work Plan that describes the Contractor's detailed approach for the performance of this contract. The work plan must be based upon this SOW. The Contractor shall review the two most recent reports for work performed for the FAA and assume that the same quality will go into the work plan. - The FAA expects that the Contractor will encounter heavy vegetation in the study areas. Old growth vegetation (assumed for purposes of this SOW as trees having a diameter of 18 inches or more at chest height) may also be encountered. If such trees are found to be present at any of the work sites, the Contractor shall coordinate with FAA and MIC to have important old growth specimens tagged. All tagged trees will be protected to the maximum extent practicable. Nevertheless, FAA expects that the Contractor will make all efforts necessary to complete the scoped activities and objectives while protecting old growth vegetation. - Clearing of vegetation is expected to the extent necessary to fully evaluate the areas of interest pursuant to this SOW. The Contractor shall use a mulching mower, brush mulcher, or similar equipment to avoid the need to haul/dispose downed vegetation. - A navigation aid outage will not be required to perform the SOW at these sites. - For all excavation confirmation laboratory samples, the Contractor shall perform Silica Gel Cleanup (SGCU) of samples by the laboratory as part of the analytical process in accordance with ADEC�s Technical Memorandum-21-001 Biogenic Interference and SGCU (December 22, 2021) to distinguish petrogenic contaminant sources from biogenic conditions. - The Contractor shall select a laboratory and processes capable of achieving sufficiently low MDLs to allow for direct comparison of analytical results to relevant CULs. - There is a discontinuous peat layer at most sites. The peat is saturated with petroleum. The peat layer when encountered and determined to be contaminated will be excavated and disposed of off island. The peat needs to be removed to help achieve reductions in the groundwater concentrations over time. - Prior investigations found that the petroleum contamination was primarily found in the top 1 to 2 feet of the AOCs, trapped in the muskeg and the top several inches of the clay layer under the muskeg. The FAA assumes that the sites will be excavated from the current edge of the pad outward and downward until extents of the petroleum contamination are found. - Prior projects encountered multiple issues due to the logistics of getting sample shipments off Annette Island and onto Gravina Island to be transported to the laboratory. The weather, airplane schedules, ferry schedules, staffing reductions and freight office closures at Alaska Airlines, can all impact the transportation of sample shipments. In order to better understand the market for this potential requirement, the FAA requests the following information from interested Small Businesses: 1. Name of Company (the resultant Prime contractor that may ultimately be awarded the subsequent contract) 2. Address 3. Point of Contact name, email address and telephone number 4. UEI Number 5. Relevant experience on similar projects within the last five years. Please provide specific contract numbers, contact names and email information to support claimed capabilities. Please submit your capability statement and the above information to Sonia.o.holguin@faa.gov no later than September 21, 2026 at 1200 Central Daylight Savings Time. Failure to respond to this pre-solicitation will preclude a Contractor�s ability to receive a copy of the future solicitation. Limit complete responses to no more than five pages. Information will not be released; however, mark PROPRIETARY on all documents submitted, as applicable.

title: Large Capacity Nonhuman Primate Cage and Rack Washer
description: This is a Notice of Intent notice. This is NOT a solicitation for proposals, proposal abstracts, or quotations. The Division of Veterinary Resources (DVR) within the National Institute of Health (NIH), Office of Research Services (ORS) requires the procurement, delivery, installation, commissioning, and training associated with the replacement of the existing Tecniplast large-capacity nonhuman primate cage and rack washer supporting nonhuman primate housing operations at the NIH main campus, Bethesda, Maryland with minimal disruption to ongoing animal care activities. DVR requires replacement of an end-of-life cage and rack washer that supports nonhuman primate (NHP) housing operations. The existing unit, manufactured by the same company that manufactures the proposed replacement system, has been in continuous service for approximately twenty (20) years and has exceeded its expected service life. The unit is experiencing increasingly frequent failures, resulting in elevated maintenance costs, operational disruptions, and material risk to research continuity. The replacement system shall provide high-capacity, pass-through washing and sanitization for NHP cages, transport equipment, racks, feeders, enrichment devices, and ancillary husbandry equipment and shall support daily cage-wash operations. All products provided under this award must support compliance with the Animal Welfare Act (AWA), Public Health Service Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, the Guide for the Care and Use of Laboratory Animals, AAALAC International Accreditation standards and Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC) requirements. This is a Notice of Intent; the National Institutes of Health (NIH) intends to negotiate a sole source contract for the Tecniplast USA model Atlantis EVO XL with: TECNIPLAST USA, INC. 1345 Enterprise Dr. West Chester, PA 19380-5964 Unique Entity Identifier (UEI): QHF3J4MS24H4 The statutory authority for this sole source requirement is 41 U.S.C. 3304(a)(1) as implemented by FAR 6.302.1(b)(1)(i) �Only One Responsible Source and No Other Supplies or Services will satisfy agency Requirements.�, no substitutions possible. Since the intent is to procure this on a sole source basis, no solicitation will be posted to Contract Opportunities, https://www.sam.gov. REQUIREMENT: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, equipment, and transportation necessary to deliver, assemble, install, commission, and validate a complete and operational large-capacity cage and rack washer system at the designated DVR NHP facility location at the NIH main campus in Bethesda, Maryland. Minimum performance requirements include: Equipment: Commercial-grade, pass-through cage and rack washer with clean and dirty side barrier operation; stainless steel construction; dual interlocked tempered-glass pass-through doors with inflatable gasket system; capacity for large NHP cages, racks, transport carts, feeders, and ancillary equipment; steam-heated operation; dedicated wash and rinse circuits; separate alkaline and acid wash tanks; automated detergent dosing; tool-free self-cleaning filtration; multiple oscillating wash arm assemblies; chamber lighting; and emergency stop devices accessible from both sides. The system must exhaust through the facility's existing HVAC system and achieve a processing cycle time of approximately 20 minutes for large NHP rack loads. Controls and Monitoring: Touchscreen operator interface with multi-level password-protected controls; remote diagnostics capability; utility monitoring and consumption tracking; data logging and export functionality; Ethernet connectivity; self-start or scheduled operation functionality; and alarm monitoring and troubleshooting. Utilities: 480V/60Hz/3-phase electrical service; steam heating; domestic water supply; facility drainage connection; exhaust integration with the facility's existing HVAC system (no independent exhaust pathway or roof penetration); temperature-controlled wastewater discharge; and pH-controlled wastewater discharge. Installation and Commissioning: Coordination with DVR and ORF personnel; pre-installation site survey; equipment delivery, assembly, installation, and utility connection; startup and commissioning; operational testing documentation; Site Acceptance Testing (SAT) verifying installation, operational performance, utility and control functionality, alarm operation, wash cycle performance, and documentation delivery. Equipment shall not be considered accepted until all SAT deficiencies are corrected. Training: Onsite training for DVR personnel covering equipment operation, routine and preventive maintenance, troubleshooting, safety features, emergency procedures, and control system reporting. Training materials to be provided electronically. Warranty: Minimum two-year manufacturer warranty covering parts, labor, travel, and technical support from date of successful commissioning and acceptance, including remote technical support and onsite service when required. Required Deliverables: Equipment submittal package; shop drawings and utility requirements; Operations and Maintenance Manuals; Preventive Maintenance Schedule; Startup and Commissioning Report; Site Acceptance Test Report; Training Documentation; and Warranty Documentation. DVR�s SPECIFIC REQUIRMENTS: DVR has two mission-essential facility-driven requirements: HVAC-Integrated Exhaust Compatibility: The current NIH DVR nonhuman primate cage washroom was designed and constructed with the cage and rack washer exhausting through the building's existing HVAC system. This infrastructure configuration does not include a dedicated roof exhaust penetration or independent exhaust duct pathway for the cage wash equipment. Processing Cycle Time: The existing cage and rack washer operates at a processing cycle time of approximately 45 minutes per load. DVR has determined this to be operationally inefficient and inadequate to support current NHP husbandry throughput requirements without scheduling constraints and delays that adversely affect daily animal care operations. DVR has established a maximum processing cycle time of approximately 20 minutes as a minimum performance requirement for the replacement system. This cycle time is necessary to process the required daily volume of NHP cage wash loads within the operational constraints of the cage washroom and DVR staffing schedules, and to restore the operational efficiency degraded by the current aging unit. Market Research (Market Research Report and Acquisition Plan, separately documented) for the replacement of the large capacity and wash rack for NHP, full and open competition, vendor neutral, performance based salient features, yielded multiple commercial manufacturers (Tecniplast USA, Getinge USA, STERIS Corporation (Amsco), Allentown Inc., Alternative Design Manufacturing and Supply and others) with established product lines of large-capacity, pass-through cage and rack washer systems designed for laboratory animal facility environments. All identified vendors offer systems that generally meet the baseline performance characteristics common to this equipment category, including pass-through barrier design, stainless steel construction, steam heating, dual wash tanks, automated detergent dosing and touchscreen controls, remote diagnostics and 480V/3-phase electrical compatibility. However, the systems (Tecniplast USA, excepted) require a dedicated, independent exhaust pathway terminating at the building exterior, typically via a roof penetration. Installing a dedicated roof exhaust for an alternative unit in the existing NIH facility would require significant structural modifications, including penetration of the roof assembly, addition of dedicated ductwork through finished building spaces, and associated mechanical and structural engineering work. These modifications would result in substantial additional cost to the Government, extended construction time

title: Basic Ordering Agreement for Steel
description: SOLICITATION EXECUTIVE SUMMARY 1. THREE-STEP PROCUREMENT FRAMEWORK The Government will procure raw metal stock and components requirements utilizing a three-step process: Step One (Combined Synopsis/Solicitation): A separate Pre-solicitation Notice will not be issued; this synopsis is combined with the solicitation on SAM.gov in accordance with FAR Subpart 12.6. Individual order-level Request for Quotes (RFQs) under this Basic Ordering Agreement (BOA) will be competed exclusively within the qualified pool and will not be synopsized, ensuring rapid execution. Clauses are in effect through FAC 2026-01. The primary NAICS code is 331110 (Iron and Steel Mills and Ferroalloy Manufacturing; Size Standard: 1,500 employees). Other codes are listed in Attachment 001 - Purchase Description, and the Product Service Code is 9515 (Plate, sheet, strip, foil, and leaf). Step Two (Master BOA Execution): The BOA Request for Proposal (RFP) will be released once for qualifications. The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors whose proposals are compliant with Section L and rated "Acceptable" under Section M. BOAs are valid for up to five (5) years. NOTE: This RFP is the only opportunity to obtain a raw metal stock and components BOA. Proposals will not be accepted or executed at any other time. If a contractor wishes to participate in any future raw metal stock and component orders, they must respond to this initial RFP. Step Three (Order-Level Competition): As recurring supply needs arise, the PCO will issue competitive, order-level RFQs to the BOA pool. To participate, contractors must hold an active master BOA as of the RFQ closing date. Orders will result in individual, competitive Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP) contracts (Orders) under FAR 16.703. 2. SCOPE Contractors will provide commercial products supporting the following CONUS sites including but not limited to: Blue Grass Army Depot (BGAD) Pine Bluff Arsenal (PBA) Letterkenny Munitions Center (LEMC) Crane Army Ammunition Activity (CAAA) Tooele Army Depot (TEAD) McAlester Army Ammunition Plant (MCAAP) Joint Manufacturing and Technology Center (JMTC) Tank-Automotive and Armaments Command (TACOM) 3. SUBCONTRACTING FLEXIBILITY Offerors must demonstrate technical capability within the scope of Attachment 001: Product Description. Capability may be achieved with or without subcontractors. In Step Three order-level proposals, contractors are not bound to the subcontractors proposed in Step Two but must propose resources necessary to perform each individual order. 4. BASIS FOR AGREEMENT EXECUTION The Government will execute no-cost, multi-award BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals (Section L) rated "Acceptable" (Section M). NOTE: The Government reserves the right to waive the Compliance Review if in its best interest. The Government intends to execute BOAs on initial proposals without discussion. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest but will only do so with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. LEGAL NOTICE: This master BOA process is not a competitive acquisition; the source selection procedures of FAR Part 15 do not apply. No pricing is requested or evaluated at this stage. Execution of a BOA does not constitute a contract or guarantee future orders. SECTION B � CONTRACT LINE-ITEM NUMBERS (CLINS) CLINs will be established at the order level for administrative categorization. SECTION C � EXECUTION BUSINESS RULES 1. GENERAL RULES The ordering period shall not exceed five (5) years from initial execution (DFARS 216.703(c)). Each BOA will be formally reviewed by the PCO annually (FAR 16.703(c)(2)) and revised as necessary. BOAs shall be changed only by modifying the agreement itself, not by individual orders. Modifications do not apply retroactively to active orders. Prior to the annual review, the PCO will confirm in writing if the contractor wishes to maintain the agreement. Either party may elect not to renew. The Government may cancel the BOA at any time if in its best interest. Only the Army Contracting Command�Rock Island Arsenal (ACC-RIA) is authorized to execute, modify, or perform annual reviews of these master BOAs. Other DoD activities may place orders under these BOAs with ACC-RIA approval. 2. STEP TWO EXECUTED BOAS (QUALIFICATION PHASE) Offerors must demonstrate technical capability by filling out Attachment 001- Purchase Description by answering �Yes� to the items that can be completed and �No� to the items that cannot be completed by offeror. The purchase description at the order level will include but is not limited to the list found in Attachment 001- Purchase Description. 3. STEP THREE ORDER REQUESTS (ORDERING PHASE) Order competitions are limited to active master BOA holders. Order performance periods will be established in each order and remain valid through completion, even if they extend beyond the master BOA's 5-year term. Specific evaluation criteria (e.g., Price-Only, LPTA, or Tradeoff) will be identified in each order�s RFQ. Detail purchase descriptions requirements will be provided at the order level. All orders will be Firm-Fixed-Price (FFP). Work shall not begin until the order is awarded. Business size standards and Non-Manufacturer Rule compliance will be certified and monitored at the order level. Offerors are required to provide pricing catalogs at the order level. SECTION H � SPECIAL CONTRACT REQUIREMENTS 1. CYBERSECURITY MATURITY MODEL CERTIFICATION (CMMC) Conditional Self-Assessment: To be eligible for award, and to remain eligible for orders, the contractor must maintain at least a conditional CMMC Level 2 Self-Assessment in the Supplier Performance Risk System (SPRS) at award. Maintenance: Failure to maintain this status will result in immediate restriction from participating in order RFQs, inability to exercise options, and potential removal from the raw metal stock and components BOA. Flow-Down: Subcontractor CMMC requirements (ranging from non-applicable to Level 2) will be defined in individual order solicitations. Primes are solely responsible for subcontractor compliance. 4. SUBCONTRACTING LIMITS AND THE NON-MANUFACTURER RULE (NMR) Limitations on Subcontracting (FAR 52.219-14): Primes must perform at least 50% of the cost of manufacturing (excluding materials) for supply orders. Non-Manufacturer Rule (FAR 52.219-33): Non-manufacturers must supply the product of a domestic small business manufacturer, unless an SBA class or individual waiver applies. The KO will monitor compliance at the order level. 5. DELIVERY PROTOCOLS Multiple Sites: Specific details will be addressed in the delivery order. 6. ANNUAL REVIEWS AND ON/OFF RAMPING The Government reserves the unilateral right to "on-ramp" (add) or "off-ramp" (remove) contractors from the BOA pool at any time based on annual review findings, performance, compliance (CMMC), or market changes. SECTION J � LIST OF ATTACHMENTS Attachment 001: Purchase Description Attachment 002: Offeror Points of Contact (POCs) Template Attachment 003: Provisions and Clauses SECTION L � INSTRUCTIONS, CONDITIONS, AND NOTICES TO OFFERORS 1. GENERAL PROPOSAL INSTRUCTIONS Review Attachment 001 �Purchase Description for insight into requirement details. Proposals must include sufficient information to demonstrate the offeror's understanding of each evaluated area. The Government intends to execute BOAs to responsible offerors with compliant proposals rated "Acceptable" for Technical. Cost/Price will not be evaluated at this stage. The Government intends to execute BOAs based on initial proposals without negotiations; initial proposals should contain complete information. The Government is not obligated to request missing data. It reserves the right to negotiate if in its best interest, but only with offerors whose proposals do not contain significant informational deficiencies. NOTICE: The source selection procedures of FAR 15.3 do not apply. Order

title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) Trailer
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

The questions due date is extended to 17 September 2026. 2) The quote due date is unchanged by this Amendment and remains 21 September 2026 at 1:00PM Central Time. 3) Update RFO Provision 52.252-3, Alterations in Solicitation. *********************************************************************************** PURPOSE: The Nashville District (LRN), U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE), is issuing a Request for Quote (RFQ) for a Firm Fixed-Price (FFP) Commercial Construction Contract for the Powerhouse Door Coating at Dale Hollow. DESCRIPTION: This procurement action is for a firm fixed-price construction contract to perform interior and exterior primer, paint, and stain removal on assembly bay door, man doors and visitor entrance doors trim and hardware. Surface repair and/or replacement of rotten and weathered wood. Stain and seal all wood on all door�s interior and exterior. Paint all metal and associate hardware black interior and exterior. PERFORMANCE LOCATION:USACE Dale Hollow Dam 305 Power House Road Celina, Tennessee 38551 Attention: Jacqueline Huff � Administrative Contracting Officer (ACO) PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE: The completion date for this contract is 140 calendar days from the receipt of Notice to Proceed (NTP). NAICS code Z1JZ and 238320 Painting and Wall Covering Contractors, Size Standard $19.0M. WHO MAY SUBMIT: This procurement is a 100% Service Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business(SDVOSB) Set-Aside. QUOTES RECEIVED BY FACSIMILE OR PHYSICAL MAIL WILL NOT BE CONSIDERED. ALL RESPONSES TO THIS ANNOUNCEMENT SHALL BE SUBMITTED ELECTRONICALLY VIA EMAIL IN ACCORDANCE WITH THE QUOTE INSTRUCTIONS. Pre-Quote Site Visit: The pre-quote site visit has been scheduled for Wednesday, 9 September 2026 at 10:00 AM Central Time (CT), near 305 Power House Road, Celine, TN 38551. The site visit request forms are attached. There will only be ONE site visit. Offerors should inspect the job site prior to submitting an offer. Offerors should take such other steps as may be reasonably necessary to ascertain the nature and location of the work and the general and local conditions that can affect the work or the cost thereof. Failure to do so will not relieve offerors from the responsibility for properly estimating the difficulty or cost of successfully performing the work. The Government assumes no responsibility for any understanding or representations concerning conditions made by any of its officers, agents or employees, unless included in the solicitation, the specifications or related documents. REGISTRATION: Only registered persons will be permitted to attend the pre-bid site visit. In addition to the information below, please also provide your firm's name, firm's CAGE and/or Unique Entity Identifier (UEI), and name and position title of primary point-of-contact and their telephone number and email address. Please provide this information via email to Jamie Lynn Barnes at Jamie.L.Barnes@usace.army.mil and Andrew Roth at andrew.r.roth@usace.army.mil. Contractors and/or potential contractors wishing to attend a pre-bid meeting held at or in LRN restricted/controlled areas (such as a Power Plant or Navigation Lock) shall submit a Nashville District (LRN) Security Access Form to the Contract Specialist five (5) days prior to the site visit. If submitting the document in less than five days, the Offeror may not receive approval for participation. The Contract Specialist will notify the Contractor if the request is approval or denied. Any pre-quote meeting which will cover anything other than public domain information shall be limited to US Citizens, except under unique circumstances. The Security Access Form and guidance is available at https://www.lrn.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Contracting. U.S. CITIZENS: The Offeror shall submit a Nashville District Corps of Engineers U.S. Citizen Security Request Form to the LRN Point of Contact, Contract Specialist Jamie Lynn Barnes via email at Jamie.L.Barnes@usace.army.mil and to the Contracting Officer Andrew Roth at Andrew.R.Roth@usace.army.mil no later than five calendar days prior to the site visit. If submitting the document in less than five days, the Offeror may not receive approval for participation. The LRN POC will notify the individual(s) if the request is approved or denied. The Security Access Form and guidance is available as a pdf attachment on sam.gov with this pre-solicitation and is titled U.S. Citizen Security Request Form. FOREIGN NATIONALS (FNs): All non-U.S. Citizens, including permanent residents wishing to attend the site visit must be approved in advance. FNs wishing to attend a site visit shall submit a completed Nashville District Corps of Engineers Foreign National Security Request Form and legible color copies of two of the following documents: Passport (unexpired or expired), Certificate of U.S. Citizenship (INS Form N-560 04 N-561), Certificate of Naturalization (INS Form N-550 or N-570), unexpired foreign Passport with 1-551 stamp or attached INS Form 1-94 indicating unexpired employment authorization, an Alien Registration Receipt Card with photo (INS Form 1-151 or 1-551), unexpired Temporary Resident Card (INS Form 1-688), unexpired Employment Authorization Card (INS Form 1-688A), unexpired Reentry Permit (INS Form 1-327), unexpired Refugee Travel Document (INS Form 1-571), or unexpired Employment Authorization Documentation issued by the INS which contains a photograph (INS Form I-688B) to the LRN Point of Contact, Contract Specialist Jamie Lynn Barnes and Contracting Officer Andrew Roth, who will forward the documents to the LRN-SM mailbox (dll-celmsm@usace.army.mil) for approval. These documents must be submitted no less than five (5) days prior to the site visit. FN requests require approval at the Headquarters U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (HQUSACE) level. Exceptions will be considered on a case-by-case basis but will be limited. The form is available as a pdf attachment on sam.gov with this solicitation and is titled Foreign National Security Request Form. ADDITIONAL INFORMATION: Specific information pertaining to this procurement will be available in the solicitation. The solicitation documents may be amended, and it is the responsibility of all potential offerors to monitor the SAM.gov website for any amendments, updates, responses to questions and answers, etc. as the Government will not be maintaining a mailing list. Information regarding the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers process for settling requests for equitable adjustments and duration goals to achieve definitization of equitable adjustments for change orders under commercial construction contracts can be found by going to https://www.usace.army.mil/Business-With-Us/Partnering/ then clicking on "View FFP Contract Changes Playbook Here".

title: Video Teleconferencing - 139th AW
description: This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial items prepared in accordance with the format in RFO FAR 12.202, as supplemented with additional information included in this notice. The solicitation number is W50S7G-26-Q-A021 and is issued as a Request for Quotation (RFQ), unless otherwise indicated herein. The associated North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 238210 with a small business size standard of $19M. This requirement is a 8(a) small business set-aside and only qualified offerors may submit quotations. The Missouri Air National Guard (139th Airlift Wing) has a requirement for Dual - Classification Video Teleconference system in Rausin Auditorium, Commanders Conference Room, Logistics Plans Work center and AATTC Room 14 & 15. Contractor will provide a full installation of a Dual-Classification system. ***Questions shall be submitted to joshua.zachariah.2@us.af.mil no later than 16 September 2026. Questions not received by this date may not be considered.*** ***There will be a site visit on 14 September 2026 @ 1:00 pm (local). Please contact joshua.zachariah.2@us.af.mil by 8 Sept to coordinate base access for the site visit. Note: All attendees will be required to submit a police record check form and provide REAL ID compliant identification in order to be granted access to the site visit location. The meeting location for this will be the Rausin Auditorium, in Bldg 51 (2nd floor).*** Project drawings will be provided, upon request, to responsible sources that are eligible to compete for this contract opportunity. For this solicitation, a responsible source is defined as a company whose primary business is the sale and/or installation of audio/video teleconferencing equipment, has a satisfactory past performance record, and is an 8(a) small business. Requests for project drawings may be submitted to joshua.zachariah.2@us.af.mil and stephen.j.miller1.civ@army.mil. Basis of Award: The basis of award will be a best value determination. A balanced evaluation approach will consider both price and discriminating non-price factors to identify the solution that results in the greatest overall benefit to the government. The Contracting Officer will determine that the awardee represents the best value (as defined in FAR 2.101) to meet the Government's needs. Vendors will be evaluated based on a comparative analysis of the quotations on the factors of (a) Price, (b) Technical Capability, and (c) Delivery Schedule. The total quoted price shall be all-inclusive to carry out the Statement of Requirements. If offeror fails to fully demonstrate quoted products and services meet the requirements, they shall be considered not technically acceptable or non-responsive. Please see the attached Request For Quotation and Statement of Requirements for specific requirement details.

The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. title: 88--Request for Information - Cattle Housing
description: THIS IS NOT A SOLICITATION FOR PROPOSALS. THIS IS A REQUEST FOR INFORMATION The Bureau of Land Management is issuing this Request for Information (RFI) to identify dairy farms and ranches with the capability and interest to provide temporary housing and care for cattle displaced by recent wildland fires. This RFI is for planning purposes only and does not constitute a solicitation or commitment for procurement. BACKGROUND Recent wildland fires have significantly impacted ranchers, creating an urgent need for alternative, short and long term cattle housing. The Government is seeking information on facilities that can provide safe, compliant, and reliable support for affected livestock for an estimated period of up to two years. REQUESTED INFORMATION Respondents are asked to provide detailed information regarding their capabilities, including: * Holding capacity (number and type of livestock that can be supported) * Timeframe and length of availability * Animal type preferences (steers, heifers, cows, bred cattle, bulls) * Location and description of facilities * Import requirements and required health certifications * Feed availability * Ability to provide feed onsite or support purchase/transportation * Capacity to store feed on site * Animal health requirements and standards maintained * Ability to separate or isolate cattle from existing herds as required * Veterinary support availability * Identification as a dairy farm or ranch operation ADDITIONAL INFORMATION This RFI is solely intended to gather information. No solicitation is anticipated to be issued, and no contract is anticipated to be awarded as a direct result of this notice. Information received may be shared with impacted ranchers and others, who may independently contact respondents if a need arises. The Capability statements shall be sent by email to judith_chamberlin@ios.doi.gov The capability statement must be submitted by Monday, September 21, 2026 at 1700ES
