title: Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services
description: SPECIAL NOTICE � UNUSUAL AND COMPELLING URGENCY Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services Notice/Requirement No.: ACQ_IHS_2026_U_01033 NAICS: 561320 � Temporary Help Services PSC: Q401 � Medical � Nursing WITHDRAWAL AND SUPERSESSION OF PREVIOUS SPECIAL NOTICE The Indian Health Service (IHS), Phoenix Area Office (PAO), is issuing this Special Notice as a follow-on to the previously published Special Notice under Notice/Requirement No. ACQ_IHS_2026_U_01033. The previous Special Notice stated the Government's intent to restrict competition based upon a determination that only one source was available. Following further review of the acquisition record, including consideration of capability information received from industry, the Government has reconsidered that determination. The Government will not proceed with an award based upon the one-source determination described in the previous Special Notice. That determination is withdrawn and superseded by the acquisition approach described in this notice. The Government's prior market research, including responses received to the public Sources Sought Notice, demonstrates meaningful industry interest in the Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services requirement. Based upon that market research, IHS intends to pursue a competitive acquisition for the longer-term requirement. The need for an interim action arose after anticipated incumbent coverage changed unexpectedly. Upon learning of the potential interruption in services, IHS initiated market research, including issuance of the public Sources Sought Notice, and pursued alternatives intended to maintain continuity while a follow-on acquisition could be developed. Those efforts did not ultimately provide sufficient coverage for the period necessary to complete and transition to the competitive follow-on acquisition. IHS therefore has an immediate need to maintain uninterrupted Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services during the period necessary to complete the competitive acquisition. Accordingly, this Special Notice provides notice of the Government's intent to pursue a limited-duration bridge action based upon unusual and compelling urgency. The bridge action described below is not based upon a determination that only one commercial source is capable of performing Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services. Rather, it is intended solely as a short-term measure to maintain continuity of services while IHS conducts and transitions to the planned competitive follow-on acquisition. NOTICE OF INTENT � LIMITED-DURATION BRIDGE REQUIREMENT The Indian Health Service (IHS), Phoenix Area Office (PAO), intends to award a limited-duration bridge contract for Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services to maintain continuity of existing clinical support services while IHS conducts a competitive acquisition for the longer-term requirement. This acquisition is being conducted pursuant to RFO FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, and 41 U.S.C. � 3304(a)(2). The Government has determined that the need for uninterrupted Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the delay necessary to complete the planned competitive acquisition before interim coverage is established would create an unacceptable risk of interruption to services supporting IHS beneficiaries. The contemplated bridge action will be limited to a six (6)-month period of performance. The duration is intended to provide only the time necessary to maintain continuity of services while IHS develops, solicits, evaluates, awards, and transitions to the competitive follow-on requirement. Consistent with the urgency authority, IHS will consider timely information received from responsible sources concerning their ability to satisfy the complete immediate bridge requirement within the timeframe available to prevent interruption of services. The Government's use of unusual and compelling urgency for this interim action does not constitute a determination that competition is unavailable for the underlying requirement and does not alter IHS's intent to competitively acquire the longer-term Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services requirement. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT IHS requires contractor-operated Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services to support eligible American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries served by the following locations: Colorado River Service Unit (CRSU), Parker, Arizona; Elko Southern Band Health Center (ELKO), Elko, Nevada; Fort Yuma Service Unit (FYSU), Winterhaven, California; and Uintah & Ouray Service Unit (U&O), Fort Duchesne, Utah. The contractor shall provide continuously available nurse telephone triage and advice-line services 24 hours per day, seven days per week, including weekends and federally recognized holidays. Services shall provide beneficiaries access to qualified Registered Nurses using nationally recognized, physician-approved, evidence-based clinical triage protocols. Based upon clinical assessment, the contractor shall provide appropriate clinical guidance and disposition, including home/self-care instructions, health education, non-emergent follow-up guidance, referrals, and direction to urgent or emergency medical care when clinically indicated. The contractor shall provide a dedicated toll-free nurse advice line and maintain the capability necessary to ensure continuous caller access. The contractor shall furnish the personnel, supervision, management, telecommunications, software, clinical protocols, and related operational support necessary to perform the requirement. Services also include appropriate documentation of patient encounters, secure transmission of required encounter information to designated IHS personnel, maintenance of applicable RN licensing and credentials, privacy and confidentiality safeguards, quality-control activities, and required performance reporting. The purpose of the requirement is to provide beneficiaries with continuous access to timely clinical assessment and guidance when facility personnel may not otherwise be immediately available and to support appropriate disposition to the level of care indicated by the beneficiary's clinical circumstances. These requirements are consistent with the underlying PWS. BASIS FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION IHS must maintain continuity of Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services while the Government develops and conducts a competitive acquisition for the longer-term requirement. The need for an interim action arose after anticipated incumbent coverage changed unexpectedly. Upon learning of the potential interruption in services, IHS initiated market research, including issuance of a public Sources Sought Notice, to identify alternative sources and assess industry capability. The Government also pursued alternatives intended to maintain continuity while developing an acquisition strategy for the follow-on requirement. Those efforts did not ultimately provide sufficient coverage for the period necessary to complete the competitive acquisition. The time presently available before continued services are required is insufficient to finalize the competitive solicitation, provide an appropriate response period, evaluate offers, make award, and complete implementation and transition activities necessary to ensure uninterrupted performance. Market research generated multiple industry responses expressing interest and providing capability information concerning the requirement. The results demonstrate meaningful industry interest and support the Government's determination that competition is appropriate for the longer-term requirement. Market research also informed the Government's acquisition strategy. title: Design-Build of a Tier II Mobile Command Post Trailer
description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) intends to award a single-award, Firm-Fixed-Price, Indefinite-Delivery/Indefinite-Quantity (IDIQ) contract for Tier II Mobile Command Post Vehicle (MCPV) systems. The purpose of this acquisition is to establish a contract vehicle for the design, engineering, manufacturing, integration, testing, and production of trailer-based mobile command post systems capable of supporting FBI command, control, communications, and computer (C4) operations. The Tier II MCPV requirement consists of a custom-integrated gooseneck trailer system and, when ordered, a compatible Class 4 prime hauler vehicle. The MCPV Trailer shall provide a mobile operational environment supporting mission communications, networking, workspace, power generation and distribution, environmental control, equipment racks, audio/visual capabilities, RF and satellite connectivity provisions, security systems, and integration of Government-furnished and Contractor-furnished mission equipment. The contract will include a First Article requirement. The Contractor shall design, manufacture, integrate, test, and obtain Government approval of an initial MCPV Trailer configuration prior to production quantities. The approved First Article configuration will establish the production baseline for subsequent MCPV Trailer systems. The Government anticipates ordering approximately thirteen (13) MCPV trailer systems and associated prime hauler vehicles over the contract ordering period; however, the Government guarantees only the minimum contract obligation identified in the solicitation. The maximum contract value shall not exceed $15,000,000.00.

title: Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services
description: SPECIAL NOTICE � UNUSUAL AND COMPELLING URGENCY Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services Notice/Requirement No.: ACQ_IHS_2026_U_01033 NAICS: 561320 � Temporary Help Services PSC: Q401 � Medical � Nursing CANCELLATION OF PREVIOUS SPECIAL NOTICE The Indian Health Service (IHS), Phoenix Area Office (PAO), hereby cancels the previously published Special Notice for Restricted Competition under Notice/Requirement No. ACQ_IHS_2026_U_01033. The previous notice stated the Government's intent to restrict competition based upon a determination that only one source was available. That notice is canceled and superseded by this Special Notice. Based upon further consideration of the Government's acquisition strategy and the market research previously conducted, IHS intends to pursue a competitive acquisition for its longer-term Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services requirement. In the interim, IHS has an immediate need to maintain continuity of the existing services. Accordingly, this Special Notice provides notice of IHS's intent to pursue a limited-duration bridge action based upon unusual and compelling urgency while the competitive follow-on acquisition is developed and conducted. NOTICE OF INTENT � LIMITED-DURATION BRIDGE REQUIREMENT The Indian Health Service (IHS), Phoenix Area Office (PAO), intends to award a limited-duration contract for Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services necessary to maintain continuity of existing clinical support services while IHS conducts a competitive acquisition for its longer-term requirement. This acquisition is being conducted pursuant to FAR 6.103-2, Unusual and Compelling Urgency, and 41 U.S.C. � 3304(a)(2), as implemented under applicable HHS Revolutionary FAR Overhaul (RFO) class deviations. The Government's need for uninterrupted Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services is of such an unusual and compelling urgency that the time required to complete a full and open competitive acquisition before continuation of services is required would create an unacceptable risk of interruption to services supporting IHS beneficiaries. DESCRIPTION OF REQUIREMENT IHS requires contractor-operated Nurse Telephone Triage and Nurse Advice Line Services supporting eligible American Indian and Alaska Native beneficiaries served by Phoenix Area facilities, including: Colorado River Service Unit, Parker, Arizona; Elko Service Unit, Elko, Nevada; Fort Yuma Service Unit, Winterhaven, California; and Uintah & Ouray Service Unit, Fort Duchesne, Utah. The required services provide beneficiaries access to Registered Nurses (RNs) using evidence-based, nationally recognized, physician-approved clinical triage protocols. Based upon clinical assessment, services may include home or self-care guidance, education regarding non-emergent appointments or prescription-renewal processes, referrals, and direction to urgent or emergency medical care, as appropriate. The requirement is for continuous telephone triage/advice-line capability to ensure beneficiaries retain access to clinical guidance when facility personnel may not otherwise be immediately available. BASIS FOR USE OF OTHER THAN FULL AND OPEN COMPETITION IHS must maintain continuity of Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services while it conducts a competitive acquisition for the longer-term requirement. The Government previously conducted market research, including issuance of a public Sources Sought Notice, and received multiple responses demonstrating industry interest in the requirement. Based upon the results of that market research, IHS intends to pursue competition for its longer-term Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line requirement. However, the time presently available before continued services are required is insufficient to complete development of the competitive solicitation, provide an appropriate solicitation response period, evaluate offers, make award, and complete the implementation and transition activities necessary for uninterrupted performance. An interruption in these services would eliminate an existing mechanism through which beneficiaries obtain after-hours and other telephone-based clinical assessment and guidance, including clinical direction concerning whether symptoms may be addressed through self-care, require follow-up with a healthcare provider, or warrant urgent or emergency medical attention. Accordingly, IHS has determined that a limited-duration bridge action is necessary to maintain continuity of these services while the Government completes the competitive acquisition. INTENDED SOURCE AND BASIS FOR LIMITING SOURCES IHS intends to solicit Risen Video Production, LLC for this limited-duration bridge requirement. Risen Video Production, LLC currently provides Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services supporting Phoenix Area operations and has existing operational capability associated with the services. Given the limited period available to prevent interruption of services, IHS has determined that utilizing the existing operational capability for the bridge period avoids transition and implementation activities that could delay continuation of services while the competitive follow-on acquisition is conducted. This determination does not represent a finding that Risen Video Production, LLC is the only commercial source capable of providing Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services. Market research identified multiple interested sources, and IHS intends to use that market information in conducting the competitive follow-on acquisition. Rather, the basis for limiting competition for this action is the immediate need to maintain continuity of services during the period necessary to conduct and transition to the competitive follow-on acquisition. PERIOD OF PERFORMANCE The anticipated period of performance for this bridge action is six (6) months. The bridge period is limited to the time the Government presently anticipates is necessary to maintain uninterrupted services while IHS conducts the competitive acquisition and transitions to the resulting follow-on contract. IHS does not intend for this bridge action to replace the planned competitive acquisition. COMPETITIVE FOLLOW-ON ACQUISITION During the bridge period, IHS intends to proceed with a competitive acquisition for its longer-term Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services requirement. Information previously received in response to the Government's Sources Sought Notice will be maintained as part of the market research supporting development of the competitive acquisition. A separate solicitation for the competitive follow-on requirement will be publicized in SAM.gov in accordance with applicable acquisition regulations and procedures. RESPONSE TO THIS NOTICE This notice is not a request for competitive proposals or quotations for the longer-term requirement. In accordance with FAR 6.103-2, the Government will consider information timely received from responsible sources regarding their ability to satisfy the immediate bridge requirement within the timeframe necessary to prevent interruption of existing services. Any responsible source that believes it can meet the Government's immediate continuity requirement without interruption to existing Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services may submit capability information for the Contracting Officer's consideration. Any such response should specifically address: the source's ability to begin full performance by the required start date; its ability to provide uninterrupted 24-hour, 7-day-per-week Nurse Telephone Triage/Nurse Advice Line Services for all required Phoenix Area locations; RN staffing and applicable licensure necessary to support the identified locations; clinical triage protocols and operational capability; implementation and transition activities required before full performance; systems, telecommunications, security, credentialing, or other infrastructure requirements aff

The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. title: Tar Lake Superfund
description: The U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) Detroit District is seeking a contractor for a Firm-Fixed Price (FFP) environmental services contract for the Tar Lake Superfund project located in Mancelona Township, Michigan. The project includes the excavation of contaminated soil and expansion of a bio-sparge system at the Tar Lake Superfund Site in Mancelona Township, Ml. The project will involve excavation of approximately 172,500 tons of contaminated soil, backfilling with clean imported soils, installing new biosparge wells, and an approximately 160 square foot pre-engineered structure to house the biosparge system compressors. Ancillary activities include abandoning existing groundwater monitoring wells, installing new groundwater monitoring wells, installing erosion control measures, conducting a utility survey to locate existing bio-sparge system piping, confirmation soil sampling,and site restoration.

title: Rapid Nicotine Pouch Data Analysis Services
description: Rapid Nicotine Pouch Data 3.1 Background FDA�s Center for Tobacco Products (CTP) regulates the manufacture, marketing, and distribution of tobacco products to protect public health and to reduce tobacco use, particularly among youth. CTP oversees the implementation of the Family Smoking Prevention and Tobacco Control Act. Some of the Agency�s responsibilities under the law include setting performance standards, reviewing premarket applications for new and modified risk tobacco products, requiring new warning labels, and establishing and enforcing advertising and promotion restrictions. On August 8, 2016, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration finalized a rule that extends its regulatory authority to all tobacco products, including e-cigarettes, cigars, and hookah and pipe tobacco, as part of its goal to improve public health. Additionally, effective April 14 (2022), Congress passed a federal law which went into effect on April 14, 2022, clarifying FDA�s authority to regulate tobacco products containing nicotine from any source, including synthetic nicotine. 3.2 Objective To effectively regulate the rapidly changing U.S. commercial tobacco and nicotine marketplace for ENDS and nicotine pouches, as required by the law, the Government intends to obtain sentinel surveillance reports summarizing findings from existing surveys and other data collection efforts aimed at obtaining rapid and sentinel information on predominant and emerging ENDs and nicotine pouch brands and tobacco use among youth and young adults. 3.3 Scope For the base period and option period 1 � 4, as outlined below, the contractor shall provide FDA with reports summarizing data from their data collection efforts related to ENDS and nicotine pouches. At a minimum, reports should include data on the following topics: (i) ENDS and nicotine pouch use overall, (ii) sources of purchase, and (iii) use by top and emerging brands among youth and young adults, and (iv) other potential topics both parties agree upon. 3.4 Tasks Task 1: Monthly Reports from Existing Online Continuous Tracking Survey of Youth and Young Adults For the base year and option years 1 � 4, the contractor shall provide a total of 12 monthly reports (1/month) summarizing findings from their existing continuous tracking survey implemented with an online sample of youth and young adults or similar data collection effort to obtain sentinel surveillance information from youth and young adults. Each monthly report shall be delivered no more than 30 days after the last day of that month (e.g., a report based on data from May 1st- May 31st, 2026, should be delivered no later than June 30th, 2026). Each monthly report shall be delivered with thorough and detailed documentation of relevant survey questions, sampling approach, data collection methods employed, and response rates achieved; data analysis methods and relevant data/analytic assumptions. The report shall include: A brief, organized summary of the key findings and overall results in a tabular format or other simple format approved by the government, A technical appendix documenting in detail the relevant survey questions, sampling approach, data collection methods employed, and response rates achieved; data analysis methods and assumptions used by the Contractor to obtain the results described; and any additional detail related to the methodology necessary to help the government appropriately interpret the key findings and overall results, PowerPoint slides with plugged aggregated monthly and quarterly estimates and charts that include youth use and brand information noted above to present the summary of the report that includes an appendix with a table of monthly estimates for each slide (wherever applicable). Task 2: Reports from Existing Nationally-Representative Longitudinal Cohort Study of Youth and Young Adults For the base year and option years 1 � 4, the contractor shall provide a total of 2 reports from each wave/data collection effort of their longitudinal cohort study implemented with a nationally representative online panel (2 reports). Each report shall be delivered no more than 30 days after the last date of data collection for that wave. Each report shall be delivered with a thorough and detailed documentation of the methodology employed for data collection and analysis. The report shall include: A brief, organized summary of the key findings and overall results in a tabular format or other simple format approved by the government, A technical appendix documenting in detail the data collection methods employed including the sampling design/approach and response rates achieved; data analytical methods and assumptions used by the Contractor to obtain the results described; and any additional detail related to the methodology necessary to help the government appropriately interpret the key findings and overall results, and A PowerPoint file PowerPoint slides with plugged aggregated monthly and quarterly estimates and charts that include survey findings to present the summary of the report. Task 3: Ad Hoc Topic-Specific Reports For the base year and option years 1 � 4, the contractor shall provide topic-specific reports (2 reports summarizing tobacco data from youth and young adults pertaining to a specific topic to be determined by the government after contract award, e.g., use of flavored tobacco products). These reports shall be delivered by the end of each base period/option year. Task 4: Meetings Kick-Off Meeting- The contractor shall participate in a project kick-off call with the CTP project team, including the COR, within 14 business days after start of the Period of Performance. The purpose of this meeting is to discuss the proposed work plan and proposed progress schedule. The contractor shall provide meeting minutes to the COR within 48 hours of meeting date. Monthly Status Meetings-The contractor shall share PowerPoint slides and meeting agenda with latest aggregated monthly and quarterly estimates at least 24 hours ahead of scheduled 30-minute monthly meetings and one-hour quarterly meetings with FDA staff (via teleconference). During these meetings, the contractor shall present and discuss deliverables completed during period; problems or issues projected or identified; and alternatives and/or recommended solution(s) for identified or projected problems or issues. The contractor shall also provide meeting minutes to FDA staff within 48 hours of meeting date. 3.5 Deliverables Monthly reports from existing online Continuous Tracking Survey of youth and young adults (12 monthly reports (1/month) for the base year and option years 1 � 4) Reports from existing nationally-Representative Longitudinal Cohort Study of youth and young adults (2 reports from each wave/data collection effort of their longitudinal cohort study implemented with a nationally representative online panel (2 reports/year) for the base year and option years 1 � 4.) Ad hoc topic-specific reports (2 reports/year for the base year and option years 1 � 4) Kickoff meeting (1 kickoff meeting) Monthly status meetings (Monthly status meetings (1/month), quarterly meetings, and meeting notes for the base year and option years 1 � 4) 3.6 Government-Furnished Property (GFP) No government furnished property will be provided to the Contractor. 3.7 Security Considerations Not applicable 3.8 Travel No travel is anticipated in the performance of this contract. 3.9 Special Material Requirements None 3.10 Other Unique Requirements and Considerations None 3.11 Place of performance It is expected that the Contractor shall perform all Task work at its own place of business. Monthly and quarterly meetings shall be held via teleconference or video conference. A kick-off meeting will be held after award via teleconference. 3.12 Period of Performance The base period is expected to be 12 months from the date of contract execution. Option Year 1 will be 12 months from the end of the base period. All subsequent

title: High Voltage Power Supplies (HVPS) for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier
description: The Government has issued an Invitation for Bid (IFB) for the fabrication, pre-acceptance storage, and delivery of six (6) High Voltage Power Supply units for the Chicago Sanitary and Ship Canal (CSSC) Electric Dispersal Barrier located in Romeoville, Illinois. PROJECT INFORMATION: This is a solicitation notice for a Non-Commercial Supply contract. The project involves the fabrication of four (4) 1.5 MW and two (2) 350 kW High Voltage Power Supplies, a mandatory twelve (12) month pre-acceptance secure storage period at the contractors facility, an option for six (6) additional months of storage, and final F.o.b. Destination delivery to the operational site. SCOPE OF WORK: The contractor shall furnish all labor, materials, and equipment necessary to manufacture, test, store, and deliver six (6) complete, fully functional HVPS units in strict accordance Scope of Work (SOW). These units are a critical component of the nations aquatic invasive species defense system. This will be a Firm Fixed Price (FFP), IFB procurement in accordance with FAR Part 14, Sealed Bidding. The Government intends to award to the lowest priced bidder deemed responsive and responsible. ACQUISITION INFORMATION: This procurement will be issued on an Unrestricted basis (Full and Open Competition). The North American Industry Classification System (NAICS) code for this procurement is 335314 (Relay and Industrial Control Manufacturing), with a corresponding small business size standard of 750 employees; this is not set-aside to small businesses. One or more of the items under this acquisition is subject to the World Trade Organization Government Procurement Agreement and Free Trade Agreements. No qualification requirement is required in order to be eligible for award; and if so, identify the office from which the qualification requirement may be obtained. All responsible sources may submit a quotation, bid, or proposal, as appropriate, which will be considered by the agency. The award is planned for fourth (4th) quarter of Fiscal Year (FY) 26.IMPORTANT POLICY: Bidders are REQUIRED to be registered and active in the System for Award Management (SAM) at www.sam.gov AT THE TIME a bid is submitted. Bidders must also be registered in the DoD Procurement Integrated Enterprise Environment (PIEE) system at https://piee.eb.mil in order to access the solicitation documents and to submit a bid in response to this Solicitation. Please include the solicitation number W912P626BA027 on all correspondence. Virtual Bid Opening: A public bid opening will be conducted virtually via Microsoft Teams at the time specified in this solicitation (21 September 2026 at 2pm ), which is one hour after the deadline for bid submission. title: Non- Standard Weapons (NSW)/ Commercially available M134D Miniguns, Mounts, Support Equipment, Spare Part Kits and Installation/Training Services
description: The purpose of this effort is to issue a sole source solicitation under Title 10 United Stated Code (U.S.C.) �3204(a)(1), as implemented by Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) 6.103-1(c)(2)(i), substantial duplication of cost to the Government that is not expected to be recovered through competition to Dillon Aero, Inc. This sole source requirement will result in a Firm Fixed Priced Indefinite Delivery Indefinite contract. The requirement for M134D Minigun weapon systems, along with associated mounting systems for various air/water/ground platforms, parts, accessories, support equipment, installation, and training for operators and maintainers. The M134D variants, including the M134D-H and M134D-M, are 7.62x51mm rotary machine guns. The Government has a need for M134D variants as they are capable of delivering precision and rapid fire on personnel and vehicle-sized (2m x 3m) materiel targets with fixed firing rates of 3,000 rounds per minute. The M134D-H is a hybrid design that utilizes titanium and skeletonized parts to offer increased weight savings of 10-20 pounds while retaining the longer service life of the steel gun. The M134D-M (marinized) variation utilizes ceramic coatings to improve corrosion resistance for use in the marine environment. Spare parts and accessories are also required for each configuration and will be incorporated into the contract. Installation and training services will be included for platform installation (air/ground/water platforms) and operator and maintainer training courses.

title: Tyndall Mess Attendant Recompete
description: This is a contract for mess attendant support services for the Berg-Liles Dining Facility which will remain under the full operational and management control of the 325th Fighter Wing Force Support Squadron (FSS), Tyndall AFB, FL. Management and operational control retained by the 325th FSS will include but is not limited to all management responsibility, oversight and decision-making authority of the day-to-day operations of the dining facility including establishing operational hours, budgeting, accounting and recordkeeping, storeroom management, and other management functions. At no time shall the contractor exercise any operational control of the dining facility in the performance of this contract. The contractor shall perform the requirements in the PWS IAW Tri-Service Food Code and conform to the professional standards identified in this contract. Furthermore, the contractor shall follow all applicable federal laws, regulations, instructions and directives as identified in the PWS. Contractor tasks include, but not limited to, the following: serving and replenishing food; cleaning interior and exterior of facilities, equipment, and utensils; maintain equipment and repair as required; preparing raw vegetables and fruits for the self-serve bars and for use by military cooks; preparing cold cuts and cheeses for the use by military cooks at the sandwich/deli bar; ensure coverage for ethnic and/or specialty food bars; make and wrap sandwiches; cut and portion pastry items and provide cashier services. description: Project: Replace Select Hot Water Heater Systems Project Number: 657-27-107 The Saint Louis, Missouri VAMC scope of work details the sequential activities for the installation of four new domestic hot water generators for heating, their commissioning, and the subsequent removal of the existing four generators. The process ensures continuous hot water service throughout the transition. 657-27-107 Replace Select Hot Water Heater Systems at The Saint Louis, Missouri VAMC as required by drawings and specifications. Pursuant to 38 USC 8127(d) and in accordance with Public Law 109-461, the Veterans Benefits, Health Care and Information Technology Act of 2006, this construction project is a competitive total set-aside for Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Businesses (SDVOSB). The project cost range is between $500,000.00 to 1,000,000.00. The North American Industry Classification Code (NAICS) for this procurement is 238220, Plumbing, Heating, and Air-Conditioning Contractors $22.0M. The duration of the project is estimated to be 120 calendar days for the base CLIN after receipt of notice to proceed. This completion period includes final inspection and clean-up. Award will be made utilizing the Best Value Lowest Price Technically Acceptable Source Selection Process in accordance with Federal Acquisition Regulation Part 15. The successful prime contractor must perform no less than 25 percent of the General Construction labor for NAICS Code 238220. Proposal submission instructions will be included in the solicitation package. The government plans to award without discussions but reserves the right to hold discussions if necessary. In accordance with FAR 52.204-7, registration in SAM (System of Award Management) is required and in accordance with Veterans Affairs Acquisition Regulation (VAAR) 802.101, prospective contractors must be registered in SAM (System of Award Management) and in the VetBiz databases under the applicable NAICS. Firms may obtain SAM information at http://www.sam.gov and VetBiz information at http://vetbiz.gov. The solicitation, including specifications and drawings, will be posted to beta.Sam.gov (https://beta.Sam.gov) on or about September 16, 2026. The offeror is responsible for monitoring and download any amendments from the Federal Business Opportunities website, which may be issued to this solicitation. The final site visit walk-through on September 22, 2026, and information session (pre-solicitation) will be scheduled, attendance is highly encouraged for any responsible sources to submit an offer which shall be considered by Department of Veterans Affairs. Location: Saint Louis VAMC JC Campus, Building #16, Room # A208 on 2nd Floor. Offers MUST confirm in writing to the CO that they plan to attend, by September 21, 2026, NLT 2PM CST. No additional site visits will be conducted for this solicitation. No hard copies of the solicitation or drawings will be provided; and telephone requests or questions will NOT be accepted. Please email requests or questions to gislaine.dorvil@va.gov , ensure that the subject line reads 657-27-107 Replace Select Hot Water Heater Systems.

title: Portable Force Plate System-Brand Name and Equal (BNE)
description: Notice of Combined Synopsis/Solicitation. This is a combined synopsis/solicitation for commercial products or commercial services prepared in accordance with part 12. This announcement constitutes the only solicitation; quotes are being requested, and a separate written solicitation will not be issued. The NAICS for this requirement is: 334519. The government is not obligated to make an award. The Government is not obligated to pay costs incurred by the Contractor during quote preparation and quote submission. Background: In collaboration with the Human-Device Interaction lab within the Office of Science and Engineering Labs (OSEL), the Division of Biomedical Physics (DBP) seeks to order a portable force plate system for gait and balance assessment. The Human-Device Interaction lab within OSEL addresses regulatory science research questions related to diagnostic, therapeutic, and assistive medical devices. Understanding human interaction with these medical devices requires biomechanics equipment that quantifies human movement. Force plate analysis is a common method by which human gait and balance can be accurately quantified. For this acquisition, a portable force plate system is needed to collect more robust, high-quality signals of human gait and balance. The system will allow for accurate quantification of subject movement. The services requested below are for the operations of the Center for Devices and Radiological Health (CDRH). Minimum Performance Requirements/ Salient Characteristics: The portable force plate system ordered must have the following salient characteristics: o A minimum of two (2) force plates capable of exporting data from at least six (6) measurement channels including force in the X, Y, and Z axes and moment in the X, Y, and Z axes. The following horizontal and vertical force and moment capacities must be met: o Force X, Y capacity must be greater than 430 Newtons. o Force Z capacity must be greater than 1300 Newtons. o Moment X, Y capacity must be greater than 225 Newton-meters. o Moment Z capacity must be greater than 80 Newton-meters. o Uses a plug & play Universal Serial Bus (USB) (2.0 or greater) interface capable of connecting and synchronizing up to 12 force plates. All cables and accessories required for synchronization should be included. O Generates digital output of at least six measurement channels (described above) that uses a single USB cable to connect with an acquisition computer running Windows 10 and is easily integrated in Vicon Nexus 2.X software. o Compatible with Vicon Nexus software versions 2.6 through 2.19 (or latest available version) o Includes necessary drivers, plugins, or SDK components for integration o Real-time data streaming capability to Vicon Nexus environment o Includes at least 15-foot USB cable for power and data transfer o Force plates allow for user selectable digital data rates between 10-1000 datasets per second. o Force plates do not require an external amplifier. Amplifier must be bult into the force plate. o Force plate dimensions are no greater than 51 x 51 x 4.6 centimeters with a 300-pound (or greater) vertical force capacity. o Force plate is portable such that it does not require any mounting and weighs less than 12 kilograms. o Hardware solutions are provided to recess the force plates into raised flooring such that data accuracy and integrity are not compromised. O The Contractor shall provide a minimum one (1) year hardware warranty from date of Government acceptance. The Contractor shall guarantee full device replacement at no additional cost to the Government for any manufacturing defects or operational failures during normal use as defined in the user manual. Warranty coverage shall include all associated shipping costs for replacement units. Place of Performance: Hardware associated with the portable force plate system to be delivered no later than 60 days after award. SHIP TO: Attn: Kimberly Kontson 10903 New Hampshire Ave Building 62-1105 Silver Spring, MD 21140 Point of contact: Kimberly Kontson Kimberly.Kontson@fda.hhs.gov Office phone: (301) 798-4990 Period of Performance: 12 consecutive months commencing upon date of award. Quotes are due by email on or before September 21, 2026, by 4:00 P.M. and should be sent to brandon.rafus@fda.hhs.gov

The required system must include, at a minimum: A 4-element hydrophone array with expansion capability to 8 elements A data acquisition system (DAQ) mounted and tested inside a pressure housing rated to 1000 meters or greater Onboard real-time detection algorithms Ability to communicate detections to an external computer Native mounting capability for the Slocum G3 glider, including attachment of the DAQ canister to the nose of the glider and hydrophones to the wings and tail The requirement includes, at a minimum, the following items: OceanObserver SNOUT V3, customized Hydrophones Hydrophone cabling Mounting hardware Glider wings SD card storage Embedded PAMLab software One year of software support Accessory kit Pelican shipping case Integration support Shipping The applicable NAICS code is 334511, Search, Detection, Navigation, Guidance, Aeronautical, and Nautical System and Instrument Manufacturing. The applicable PSC is 6640. This notice is issued solely for market research purposes to determine whether other responsible sources can satisfy the Government�s minimum requirements.
